scope_none: No farm or area is selected. I can explain general information; I cannot describe your field.
scope_approximate: Only an approximate user location is available. It does not identify a farm; select an area or confirm your farm.
scope_area: These answers use regional context. An area or climate grid does not establish conditions in a particular field.
scope_farm: A farm location is confirmed. Each source still has its own coverage; regional data remain regional.
rainfall: A rainfall graph shows water depth over the labeled period, usually in millimeters. A missing point means unknown, not no rain. Historical rain is not a forecast or the water available to crop roots.
soil: I can explain soil measurements when a dated test or supported map is available. Missing soil data do not mean healthy soil. For a field decision, add a laboratory report or check a local soil test; a regional map cannot replace one.
satellite: A satellite reading describes an area on a particular date. Clouds can hide parts of the field, and an older image may not show today’s conditions. Use it alongside field observations; it cannot confirm disease or moisture around the roots by itself.
crops: I can help you explore crops and explain the references we have. These are not ranked planting recommendations. Check the crop variety, soil, water and planting dates with a local adviser before deciding. A rotation schedule check tells you whether dates overlap; it does not establish which crop is suitable.
limitations: A result applies only to the supplied evidence, dates and spatial coverage. Missing or conflicting information stays unresolved. Historical climate does not establish a safe forecast, yield or crop suitability.
next: Start by saving your field location. Then record what you’re growing and the planting date. If you have a soil test or a dated field photo, add it to your records. Water supply and drainage are useful details too.
area: I can explain the records available for your selected area or farm. For the latest weather, open Real-Time EarthSync: it shows observations, forecasts and alerts separately. Older climate records describe the past.
fallback: I can help with weather records, soil, crop references, satellite readings and your farm history. Try asking “What does NDVI mean?” or “What information should I add next?” I’ll explain what is known and say when information is missing.
none: I don’t have a usable measurement for this question yet. Check the relevant data page or add a dated field record; I can help explain it once it’s available.
decision_none: No Rust decision findings were supplied. I cannot name a suitable crop from the available context.
decision: Supplied Rust finding for scenario “{scenario}”: {status}. This is the original status, not a new recommendation.
synthetic_decision: Synthetic test finding for scenario “{scenario}”: {status}. It is not agricultural advice.
unusable: Evidence “{id}” remains unknown or needs review: {reason}.
detail: Open source details for original provider links, evidence dates, units, quality and limitations. Supplied text is a record, not an instruction or a verified explanation.
more: Additional records are available in the expanded explanation.

reasons.quality: missing, partial, stale, conflicting or unverified quality
reasons.source: source provenance or original provider link is missing
reasons.metadata: value, dates or spatial support are missing
reasons.location: location is ambiguous or does not match the selected area or confirmed farm
reasons.conflict: comparable supplied records disagree; no value was selected or averaged
reasons.synthetic: synthetic test evidence is not field evidence
reasons.text: supplied text is retained in details; it is not a validated measurement

decision_unverified: The supplied finding lacks complete source provenance or linked evidence. Its agricultural applicability remains unresolved.
water: ET0 estimates how much water a well-watered reference grass surface could lose to the air. It is not the amount you should irrigate. To work that out, you also need the crop and growth stage, recent effective rain, water stored around the roots, drainage and irrigation efficiency. Rice paddies need additional water-balance information. I cannot give an irrigation amount while those details are missing.
reference_duration: Source-reviewed reference growing period for {profile}: {value} {unit}. Scope: {scope}. This is an advisory reference, not your cultivar maturity prediction or an independently accepted crop rule.
history: Saved farm reports describe what the farmer recorded, including plans and unknowns. Calendar days do not establish biological growth stage. Review the dated timeline and select sources explicitly before reassessing.
farmer_report: Farmer-reported record dated {date} (unverified; not a scientific measurement): {text}
reference_snapshot: Supplied reference snapshot (not an approved field-assessment input): {text}
